basis: Defining skin/nail, limb and dental abnormalities; nasolacrimal obstruction in 80-99% supports ocular involvement.
Defining cardiac, neurodevelopmental and urinary malformations; dental anomalies in 80-99%. Hearing loss and skeletal defects (30-79%) omitted under cap.
Lymphoid-cell malignancy arising in the tonsil, within the pharyngeal airway; lymphoma warrants the immune mechanism axis.
Congenital pulmonary artery origin defect; respiratory symptoms do not establish intrinsic lung damage. Pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in only 1-4%.
CITED2-associated atrial septal malformation; anomalous pulmonary venous return is also cardiovascular.
Chronic intestinal motility failure defines the condition; seizures, spastic diplegia and hydronephrosis are each reported in only 5-29%.
Congenital brain malformations with developmental disability and epilepsy; optic nerve hypoplasia occurs in only 5-29%; strabismus alone lacks intrinsic eye damage.
Carcinoma arising in the pharynx, explicitly included in the pulmonary axis.
Acute infection and inflammation of the renal parenchyma and collecting system.
Isolated familial myocardial disease causing ventricular dilation, impaired contractility and heart failure.
Crossed renal ectopia is a defining urinary malformation; pelvic internal fat proliferation does not establish skin or endocrine disease.
Umbrella of congenital cortical and other brain malformations; extra-neurologic abnormalities are subtype-dependent.
Low-grade neuroendocrine tumor originating in the ileum; neuroendocrine histology alone does not establish endocrine gland disease.
Carcinoma arising in an adrenal endocrine gland.
Atypical lymphoid-cell proliferation defines a hematological disorder; the concept does not establish lymphoma or a specific immune-mediated cause.
Autoimmune blistering disease; damaging oral mucosal erosions occur in roughly half overall, predominantly in pemphigus vulgaris; other mucosal sites are less common.
Hereditary sensory and autonomic peripheral neuropathy; associated loss of smell also belongs to the neurologic axis.
Localized lung tissue lesion; its varied possible causes do not establish infection or another mechanism for the umbrella concept.
Immunodeficiency with thrombocytopenia; bronchiectasis in 3/6 and oral ulcers in 4/6. Pyoderma gangrenosum in 2/6 omitted under cap.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; vestibular dysfunction also falls within the otologic axis.
Respiratory-chain metabolic disorder; developmental disability, cardiomyopathy and pigmentary retinopathy each in 1/1 reported patient. Muscle/liver frequencies unknown; cap reached.
Defining diaphragm defect, short bowel and absent spleen; congenital diaphragmatic hernia commonly causes pulmonary hypoplasia (>30%), though syndrome-specific frequency is unavailable.
Benign neoplasm confined to the vagina, a reproductive organ outside these axes; definition explicitly excludes an HPV association.
Defined by endocrine dysfunction, obesity, hypogonadism and growth hormone deficiency together with developmental delay and intellectual disability.
Sideroblastic anemia is a disorder of erythropoiesis; pyridoxine responsiveness alone does not establish systemic metabolic or other organ damage.
